images.title: Zero holds a place
images.purpose: Show that a place the name skips must be filled with a 0 when the number is written.
images.composition: A ticket with the name on top, a one-row chart in the middle with two tagged zero cells, and the number below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Top: a ticket, a wide rounded rectangle about 1150 by 130 px with a small semicircular notch cut in the middle of its left end and of its right end, a thin dark outline and a plain white fill, with the one line Sixty thousand two hundred nine in dark text (50 px). Middle: a chart of 5 columns about 210 px wide and 2 rows. Header row: TTh, Th, H, T, O in white bold letters on blue #0072B2 cells. Digit row: 6, 0, 2, 0, 9 in large bold dark numerals (90 px). The two 0 cells (under Th and under T) have a reddish purple #CC79A7 fill; the cells holding 6, 2 and 9 are white. Under each of the two 0 cells a small tag reading no word, so write 0 (34 px, dark) with a short tick pointing up to its cell. Bottom: the number 60,209 in very large bold dark numerals (120 px) with the comma clear.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: When the name has no word for a place, write 0 in that place so every digit stays where it belongs.
images.description: A ticket reading Sixty thousand two hundred nine above a place value chart with digits 6, 0, 2, 0, 9, where the two zeros are highlighted and tagged no word, so write 0, and the number 60,209 below.
images.context: Concept image for Zero holds a place when we write. The figure in your maths book fills the empty places of forty thousand eight with zeros; this image uses the video's own example, 60,209.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many digits the number must have. Five places must all be filled, so each place the name does not mention gets a 0. Compare with leaving the zeros out, which would give a smaller number with fewer digits.

image_decisions.why: A chart with the skipped places shown as zeros stops students from dropping zeros when they write.
